sw_walker.text: Portpatrick to Cockburnspath, two hundred and twelve miles. I am doing it in sections, which is what you call it when you keep going home for a bath.
The best bit is the day nobody warned me about. It is different every time.

sw_librarian.text: The miners here set up their own library, and paid for it themselves. I like to say they dug for lead by day and for ideas by night. It does not always go down well.
Down the mine they worked by candle. Up here we have electricity, but we have not let it go to our heads.

sw_landlady.text: We have had walkers, writers and a surprising number of wet dogs. The fire has seen them all. Tibbie would have approved of the fire.
Mòran taing for stopping. Mind the sheep on your way out. They have opinions.

sw_shepherd.text: There are more sheep on this hill than people in the whole county, and they all know where the gap in the wall is. It is a gift.
If one of them looks at you, that is not an invitation to conversation. It is an invitation to leave.
